title: Virtual environments
text: A virtual environment keeps project dependencies isolated from the system Python. Create one with the standard library module: python -m venv .venv. On Windows activate it with .venv\Scripts\activate, and on Linux or macOS use source .venv/bin/activate. Inside the environment, pip installs packages locally so different projects can pin different versions without conflict. Deactivate with the deactivate command.

title: Installing packages with pip
text: pip is Python's package installer. Run pip install requests to fetch a package from the index, or pip install -r requirements.txt to install every pinned dependency a project declares. Pin exact versions such as numpy==2.5.2 in requirements.txt so builds stay reproducible. pip freeze writes the current environment to a file, and pip show displays metadata about an installed package.

title: Testing with pytest
text: pytest discovers tests named test_*.py automatically. Run the whole suite with python -m pytest tests/ -q for quiet output. Each test is a plain function that asserts expectations; use pytest.raises to assert that a function raises a specific exception with a matching message. Markers, fixtures, and parametrisation extend the basic assert style, and the exit code is zero when every test passes.

title: List comprehensions
text: A list comprehension builds a list in one expression: squares = [x * x for x in range(10)]. Add an if clause to filter: evens = [x for x in numbers if x % 2 == 0]. Comprehensions are faster and clearer than appending inside a for loop, but keep them short; a deeply nested comprehension hurts readability, so fall back to a plain loop when the logic grows.

A decorator wraps a function to add behaviour without editing its body. The at-sign syntax decorator(name) placed above a definition is sugar for reassigning the function through the wrapper. Common examples log call timing, check permissions, or cache results. Decorators receive the original function and return a replacement, so the decorated name now refers to the wrapper returned by the decorator.
title: Decorators
Generators and yield
text: A generator function yields values one at a time instead of building a whole list. Calling the function returns an iterator that pauses at each yield, which keeps memory usage flat even for huge inputs. The for statement drives the iterator automatically, and the next function pulls one value. Generators shine for streaming files, pipelines, and any loop where you only need one item at a time.

title: Dictionaries
text: A dictionary maps keys to values with average constant-time lookup. Access a key with brackets, which raises a KeyError when it is missing, or use get with a default value to avoid the error. Dictionaries preserve insertion order in modern Python, so iteration follows the order items were added. Comprehension syntax also builds dictionaries, for example {k: v for k, v in pairs}.

title: Command line arguments with argparse
text: The argparse module parses command line flags into a namespace. Define options such as --demo, --file, or --epochs with add_argument, then call parse_args. Boolean flags use action equals store_true, and mutually exclusive groups express either-or choices. When a required action is missing, call parser.error to exit with code two and a helpful message instead of crashing later.

title: Exceptions and error handling
text: Exceptions separate error handling from normal flow. Wrap risky code in try, handle failures in except, run cleanup in finally, and use else for code that runs only when no exception occurred. Raise your own errors with raise ValueError('message') to report invalid input. Catch the narrowest exception you can handle, because a bare except hides real bugs.
